articles.title: Birkenstock Preps for Winter With Two Cozy Loma and Solana Silhouettes
articles.description: Name: Birkenstock Loma, SolanaColorway: “Cork Brown”SKU: 26093610000830, 26093610000930MSRP: ¥27,500 JPY (approx. $174 USD)Release Date: November 2026Where to Buy: JOURNAL STANDARD RakutenBirkenstock and JOURNAL STANDARD introduce two exclusive cold-weather styles, bringing the Loma and Solana together in a shared “Cork Brown” treatment. The Loma takes the more enclosed approach, pairing a rounded closed toe with a broad suede strap across the instep, while the Solana opens up the forefoot with a wide single-strap construction for a more relaxed slide profile. Across both, the warm caramel-brown suede has a softly brushed, matte finish that gives the shoes a slightly lived-in character, with subtle tonal variation across the nap. The monochrome treatment keeps stitching and edge details understated, while the dark outsole creates a slim visual break beneath the otherwise earthy upper. The seasonal release is defined most clearly by its plush lamb-wool lining, which fills the footbed and wraps around the interior edges in a deeper, fuzzy brown tone. That contrast between the smooth suede exterior and dense shearling-like interior gives both silhouettes a warmer, more tactile presence without dramatically changing their minimal Birkenstock shapes. The Loma’s extra coverage makes the treatment feel closer to a winter clog, while the Solana retains more of the ease and openness of a traditional sandal. Both JOURNAL STANDARD-exclusive models are available for pre-order now in Japan, with deliveries scheduled to begin in mid-November 2026. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

articles.title: Ethereum consolidates around key technical levels amid a challenging macro backdrop. What to watch next?
articles.description: Ethereum has been consolidating around key technical levels as the negative macro backdrop continues to weigh on the crypto market. Meanwhile, the geopolitical situation remains unchanged amid stalled US-Iran negotiations and the ongoing Saudi-Houthi conflict. Oil prices are back above the $100 level, the Federal Reserve can only get more hawkish amid higher inflation and growth concerns are starting to take centre stage. That’s a bad mix for risk assets like Ethereum. This week, the most important event will likely be the release of the US Flash PMIs on Friday, barring a surprising breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations. If the data disappoints, growth concerns will likely increase, and we could see another selloff in Ethereum. Better than expected data, on the other hand, might lead to a relief rally in the short-term but it wouldn’t change the bigger picture as it would just reinforce the need for rate hikes. ETHEREUM TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME On the daily chart, we can see that Ethereumis consolidating around the major 2,360 support and the trendline. The buyers will likely continue to step in around these levels, with a defined risk below the trendline, to keep targeting the 3,400 level. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking lower to open the door for new lows and target the 1,900 level next. ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 4 hour chart, we have a downward trendline defining the bearish structure. We can expect the sellers to continue to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting a break below the major upward trendline. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to increase the bullish bets into new highs, with the 2,570 level as the first target. ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here as the buyers will continue to step in around the support and the upward trendline or wait for a break above the downward one to position for new highs, while the sellers will need a break below the upward trendline to open the door for ne lows. The red lines define the average daily range for today. UPCOMING CATALYSTS On Thursday we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures, while on Friday we conclude the week with the Flash US PMIs. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

articles.title: XTB Opens Investing Accounts to Teenagers, Starting in Romania
articles.sourceName: Financial And Business News | Finance Magnates
articles.description: XTB launched investing accounts for 14- to 17-year-olds in Romania today (Tuesday), with parents keeping control of the money. Romania is the first country to get the service, called XTB Young, the Polish broker said. Clients aged 18 to 24 made up 17.4% of XTB's active clients across all its markets in the first half of 2026. In Romania, about a fifth of the broker's users are under 30. The new accounts reach customers before they turn 18. At that point the account can continue under the parent's mandate, or the young person can open a standard XTB account, the broker said. London's trading industry is coming home! Parents Hold the Money, Teenagers Place the Trades Teenagers can buy shares, including fractional shares, and exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Only a parent or legal guardian can deposit, withdraw or transfer funds, and deposits are capped at RON 15,000 (about $3,160) a year per account. The teenager opens and closes positions. The parent sees each account separately in real time, gets an alert on every trade and can close any position the teenager has opened. One parent may open up to three accounts. Leverage and contracts for difference (CFDs) are off limits. Commodity CFDs alone generated 60.5% of XTB's gross result from financial instruments in Q2 2026, FM Intelligence data show. ETF-based Investment Plans, which XTB redesigned and rolled out in five European markets in July, are available to teenagers in Romania. To activate an account, the parent signs a legal guardian declaration and a power of attorney electronically. Contracts, statements and tax reports go to the parent, and the app includes learning material and an AI assistant, XTB said. Brokers Look for Clients Before They Turn 18 The broker tied the launch to a survey it commissioned from Reveal Marketing Research in May. In it, 44% of respondents said money was discussed at home only when necessary during their childhood, and 12% said it was a sensitive or taboo subject. Irina Cristescu, general manager of XTB Romania, said starting early is an advantage because "you have more time to learn from mistakes." Charles Schwab opened a Teen Investor Account in the US in March for 13- to 17-year-olds. It is held jointly with a parent and also allows stocks, fractional shares and most ETFs, while options, futures, forex and leveraged ETFs are excluded, according to Schwab. In Germany, Trade Republic started a children's securities account in May 2025, initially for those under 16 and managed by parents, the personal finance site Finanztip reported. The two brokers compete in each other's home markets, and XTB's chief executive said in June it would spend more on marketing in Germany than in Poland this year. In the UK, CMC Markets added a Junior Cash ISA in April paying a variable 3.56%, a savings product with no share trading. XTB, which has sold ISAs in the UK since December 2024, is campaigning there to lower the age for opening and managing a Stocks and Shares ISA alone from 18 to 16. This article was written by Damian Chmiel at www.financemagnates.com.

articles.description: Audi has introduced the third-generation Q5 in South Africa, strengthening its presence in the competitive premium mid-size SUV segment dominated by established rivals including the BMW X3, X4 and Mercedes-Benz GLC. The latest Q5 arrives as the German premium manufacturer continues renewing its SUV portfolio under its “Q: A New Era” campaign, following the local introduction of the new Q3 in July. Audi South Africa also plans to introduce the next-generation Q7 and the new Q9 in 2027, further expanding its offering in a market where SUVs account for a significant proportion of premium vehicle sales. READ: Audi unveils all-new Q7 as luxury SUV battle heats up The Q5 nameplate made its South African debut in 2009, following the global introduction of the first-generation model in 2008. The latest generation brings revised styling, upgraded technology and a new vehicle platform. SUVs dominate premium market According to Audi South Africa, SUVs account for approximately 65% of premium vehicle sales, with the mid-size SUV category representing around 30% of the market. The segment includes established competitors such as the BMW X3, Mercedes-Benz GLC and Volvo XC60. Audi South Africa’s head of retail, planning and supply chain Asif Hoosen said conventional SUVs account for 61% of the broader premium SUV market, compared with 39% for coupé-inspired Sportback models. However, Audi’s own customer preferences reflect a different trend, with Sportback models accounting for 56% of its SUV demand. Gauteng remains the country’s largest premium vehicle market, accounting for approximately 53% of sales. The Western Cape and KwaZulu-Natal each account for around 17%, with the former identified as a growing market. New technology and engine options The Q5 becomes Audi’s first SUV built on its Premium Platform Combustion architecture, designed to accommodate updated combustion engines and electrification technologies. Three powertrains are available, including a 2.0-litre turbodiesel producing 150kW and 400Nm, a 2.0-litre turbo-petrol delivering 200kW and 400Nm, and a performance-focused 3.0-litre V6 petrol engine producing 270kW and 550Nm in the SQ5. The diesel benefits from mild-hybrid technology, while chassis improvements include brake torque vectoring and available adaptive air suspension. Inside, the Q5 features Audi’s panoramic OLED digital display, with an optional passenger screen offering entertainment and gaming functionality. Additional technologies include an upgraded head-up display and second-generation digital OLED taillights with proximity detection and communication functions. Pricing strategy raises questions Pricing starts at R1,275,000 for the Q5 TDI Sportback, while the petrol-powered Q5 SUV starts at R1,295,000. The petrol Sportback starts at R1,365,000, while the performance-oriented SQ5 SUV is priced from R1,510,000. This positions the Q5 above several entry-level competitors. For comparison, the BMW X3 xDrive20d starts at approximately R1.064 million, while the Mercedes-Benz GLC 220d is priced from R1,047,850; and R1,058,400 for the Volvo XC60. However, Audi has positioned the entry-level SQ5 approximately R40,000 below the BMW X3 M50 xDrive, potentially making it an attractive alternative for performance-focused buyers. READ: BMW boosts X3 M50 power, adds new Black Package First driving impressions During the Western Cape media launch, Sunday World sampled the Q5 TDI Sportback and SQ5 on a route through Paarl, Du Toitskloof Pass and the Franschhoek Valley. The diesel impressed with its quiet operation, particularly in urban environments, while displaying composed handling and balanced driving characteristics. Fuel consumption averaged 7.6 litres per 100km against Audi’s claimed 5.1 litres. However, the relatively short driving period was insufficient for a conclusive efficiency assessment. The cabin’s digital displays were impressive, although certain controls appeared less contemporary than those in the recently launched Q3. The SQ5 delivered responsive acceleration and engaging handling, accompanied by occasional exhaust crackles and pops. Its V6 soundtrack, however, was less pronounced than expected. Overall, the new Q5 appears well equipped to compete in South Africa’s premium SUV market, although a longer road test will provide a clearer assessment of its efficiency, practicality and everyday performance.
